questions.q: What does Al-Faruq, Umar's title, mean?
options: The one who distinguishes truth from falsehood
questions.explain: A title from the Prophet SAW.

options: The title of the Muslims' leader, like Umar as caliph

questions.explain: Umar arrived with his sword, the Prophet SAW held his collar, and Umar embraced Islam.

questions.q: Why do bonds between Muslims grow stronger when numbers are small?
options: Because they were of one tribe
Because of shared pressure and a shared mission

questions.q: What did Umar remember as caliph about his past?
options: His days as a shepherd and his father's harshness

questions.q: Hamzah planned for a long time before embracing Islam.
questions.explain: False. Hamzah did not plan it; Allah opened his heart.

questions.q: Umar was busy with grand matters until he was reminded that his own sister had embraced Islam.
questions.explain: True. Settle the matters of your own house.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Umar bathes and reads Surah Taha
Umar strikes his sister and is moved
Umar sets out with his sword

questions.explain: Hamzah embraced Islam, Umar set out with his sword, struck his sister, read Taha, then embraced Islam.

One who holds to the upright religion of Ibrahim

questions.explain: Kabilah is a tribe, ukhuwah is brotherhood, suhuf are Quran sheets, and a hanif holds to Ibrahim's religion.

questions.q: Umar asked why they hid if they were on the truth. What is the lesson?
options: Be bold in showing the truth
